citation.author: Andrew Westerside & Jussi Holopainen
citation.title: Sites of Play: Locating Gameplace in Red Dead Redemption 2
citation.venue: Proceedings of DiGRA 2019 (Digital Games Research Association)

discipline: Performance studies x games design research (HCI bias)
thesis: RDR2 makes place qua place its central compositional resource; the critical vocabulary of site-specific performance studies, transposed via the coined term 'gameplace' (the affective relationship between place, experience, and play), best accounts for how the game generates affect, emotional response, and player identification, with place functioning as both topopoetic storyteller and structural ballast.
sections: Site as Storyteller, Site as Structure

concepts.gloss: The affective relationship between place, experience and play; defined against the merely navigable gameworld, and refining Ali (2016) by foregrounding how ludic elements (activities, goals, narrative) make a place mean.
Nitsche's three indicators of placeness (identity; self-motivated and self-organised action; traces of memory), read as overlapping with site-specific performance's notion of site.
After Tuan (1977): space becomes place when filled or woven through with human connections; a fundamentally human difference licensing games-in-places as site-specific encounters.
McLucas's term (via Kaye 2000): a place and what is built there bleed into each other, constituting another order of existence; supplies the place/space ontological differentiation.
Casey's poetic truth of place rather than topographical representation; RDR2 claimed as the most explicit and abundant example in videogames.
Wilkie's taxonomy of how site-specific work engages site, applied to RDR2's three-place geographic narrative.
concepts.locus: Go West / Site as Structure (Wilkie, 2002, p.158)

concepts.gloss: Pearson's taxonomy of the visitor, mapped onto RDR2 traversal and encounter: nomad (paths over places), wayfarer (mini-map), derivist (chance encounters), flaneur (loitering witness).
Friction between free-roaming (Arthur as vessel of player's objectives) and story quests (which remove agency and impose Arthur's fictional agency), yielding identification with vs. as Arthur.
After Wark (2007): regions compressed into caricatures rather than accurate representations (contra Schwartz 2006); the order of encounter is itself an affective device.
A gameworld is space for traversal; a gameplace is a world for being in — the key distinction the article draws.

readings.claim: RDR2 deploys Jenkins's four modes of environmental storytelling (evocative spaces, enacting stories, embedded narratives, emergent narratives), whose interweaving builds a believable, place-saturated gameworld.
Where RDR used the Western as a conduit of neoliberal ideology (Humphreys), RDR2 makes the frontier itself the political ideal and lets outlaw Arthur Morgan escape Marston's recuperation-critique.

The three-place geographic narrative (blizzard mountains -> Valentine -> Saint Denis) stages a wrenching dissonance between three orders of existence produced by the iterative, compressed relation to landscape.
readings.locus: Site as Storyteller, Site as Structure

readings.claim: Arthur's 'man out of time' / 'more ghosts than people' sentiment is keyed to place and carries curious parallels to the post-truth era.
RDR2's realism resides in pedestrian domestic minutiae and NPC activity rather than graphical fidelity; the world appears to exist in spite of us.
The places and regions of RDR2 perform topopoesis, coming together as poetic places that reveal something affective and human.

game_elements.how_treated: Evocative spaces evoking southern US archetypes (Louisiana swamps, Texan oilfields); affect driven by spatial compression (Grizzlies to Lemoyne in under 10 minutes) and the order of encounter, not accurate representation.
game_elements.locus: Go West; Site as Structure; endnote 4

game_elements.how_treated: Low-visibility, scarce-resource opening that codes the gang as nomadic/refugee; site as 'story-teller-in-chief'; takes over an hour to escape on first playthrough, making safety inconceivable.

Quintessential frontier town (saloon, jail, stables, hotel, train station) drawing on Leone/Ford/Westworld/Hudson River School/Sargent; site where the player gets the first window into Arthur because it looks exactly as the Old West is expected to look.

Steel-and-steam town with streetlights, cobbled streets, theatres, factories, public transport; emergence feels almost magical/inconceivable; arrival is the empathy-driven climax of feeling and exemplifies site-as-structure.

Gang's base of operations relocates across the map yet remains the place of care, maintenance, and familial interaction; acts as home for the player; anchors the expanded (political) sense of home via Wright's open-frontier cowboy myth.

game_elements.element: Traversal & encounter systems (mini-map vs. random encounter)
game_elements.how_treated: Mini-map 'dot' = player as wayfarer; NPC-call or crowd-drawn random encounter = player as derivist; near-continuous control builds a kinaesthetic bond with the avatar.
Camps, towns, city teem with goal-bearing NPCs; background chatter signals meaningful activity independent of the player; varying believability (Mateas; Tanenbaum); player as flaneur.
Hunting (big game), poker, theatre, exploration; compendium/achievement systems and Arthur's personal journal scaffold self-set long-term goals, marking the gameworld as a world for being in.

Positive/negative actions shift NPC behavior, vendor prices, dialogue trees; robbery/murder most dishonorable; the unique exception is gaining positive honor for punishing a KKK meeting (a crime judged by future ethics).

As prequel to a game that kills the gang and lacks Arthur, RDR2 is haunted by Arthur's death (confirmed by his Ch.5 tuberculosis), both galvanizing and diminishing self-motivated investment in emergent narrative.

themes: the mythic American frontier / Western genre

interlocutors.name: Edward S. Casey

interlocutors.name: Yi-Fu Tuan

interlocutors.name: Soraya Murray

interlocutors.name: Henry Jenkins

debate_axis_positions: Phenomenology/experience-of-place over straight ideology-critique: engages Humphreys but shifts the axis to how place is affectively experienced; reads RDR2 as partly escaping the neoliberal recuperation pinned on RDR (concedes the critique's force).

Qualitative close-reading over empirical user study: grounds claims in 30+ hours of reflective first-person play (Bizzocchi & Tanenbaum), taking the interpretive-humanities pole versus the cluster's HCI/UX-measurement members.
Disciplinary import: transplants performance studies (site-specific theory) into game analysis, making place/site the bridge concept.
Internal games-studies refinement: sharpens gameworld (traversable space) vs. gameplace (lived, affect-bearing place), extending Nitsche's placeness toward a ludic-affective account.
tensions: Free-roam vs. story-quest friction: the dual mode of agency both empowers the player (self-motivated desire) and revokes agency (imposed protagonist agency) — an unresolved productive tension in identification (with vs. as Arthur).
Galvanize vs. diminish: the prequel-haunting of Arthur's foreknown death simultaneously intensifies and deflates the drive to pursue emergent narrative (endnote 5).
Method warning: single-author surname overlap — 'Wright' here is sociologist Will Wright (2001), distinct from the cluster's Wright (2021); not a cluster citation.

Affect vs. ideology: the article leans toward affect/phenomenology yet leaves partly open whether RDR2's frontier-as-ideal merely re-codes (rather than escapes) the neoliberal myth it critiques in RDR.
Conference-paper depth: rich close-reading but no empirical/quantitative grounding; generalization to other genres is gestured at (future work) rather than demonstrated.
